question: Explain the formation of spherical and plane wavefronts using Huygens principle. Hence justify why light from a very distant source may be treated as a plane wavefront near the observer.

options.A: A point source forms a plane wavefront because all points have equal phase. A distant source makes the wavefront more curved near observer.
options.B: A point source emits in all directions; after time $t$, points reached at equal distance $vt$ form a spherical wavefront. For a very distant source, the arriving spherical wavefront has very large radius, so over a small region near the observer its curvature is negligible and it may be treated as a plane wavefront.
options.C: Spherical wavefronts arise only when the medium is non-homogeneous, while plane wavefronts arise only at the source.
options.D: All light wavefronts are exactly plane because light always travels along straight rays.
